description: Search the Pokémon TCG card catalogue by name, set, print region, rarity, artist or release window. Returns one row per printing with its set, rarity, illustrator and euro price index. Print regions are WEST (176 sets), JP (379 sets) and CN (96 sets, Simplified Chinese), measured 2026-09-16. Japanese sets are not translations of Western ones: they have their own boundaries, their own numbering and their own release dates, so a Japanese set and its international counterpart are two different rows. Card names exist in eight locales, and they are far from equally filled. Measured 2026-09-16 against 57,450 cards: en 57,421, fr 42,858, de 42,604, ja 27,230, it 21,644, es 21,003, pt 13,822, zh 3,492. Passing lang= replaces the name field itself and falls back to English when a translation is missing, so a thin locale answers mostly in English. Set names are not translated. Card game text is present since 2026-09-03, in English, and unevenly. Measured 2026-09-16: attacks on 29.9% of the catalogue, subtypes on 35.0%, weaknesses on 28.0%, flavor_text on 17.9%, abilities on 7.0%, rules on 5.1%. It sits on the 20,725 Western printings, so read against those alone attacks is on 82.9% of them, while Japanese and Chinese printings carry none. Check the field on the card in hand rather than assuming: a null attacks means we do not hold it, never that the card has no attack. Still empty for every card: level, and legalities — deck legality is a question this API cannot answer, so say so rather than inferring it. If the result carries next_step, show its handoff sentence and URL to the user verbatim and do not retry.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous call. Never construct one.

lang.description: Return card names in this locale.

name.description: Card name or part of it, e.g. "charizard".

order_by.description: e.g. "-set.releaseDate", "name". Sorting always ends with id.

q.description: Escape hatch: raw Lucene-style query. Field names are camelCase and dotted (set.code, set.releaseDate, nationalPokedexNumbers) while response keys are snake_case. Only use this when the named arguments above cannot express the question.

rarity.description: Exact printed rarity. Use ptcg_get_reference to list valid values.

region.description: Print region of the set the card belongs to.

released_from.description: ISO date, inclusive lower bound on the set release date.

released_to.description: ISO date, inclusive upper bound on the set release date.

set.description: Set code, e.g. "bs", "sv3", or several separated by commas. Use ptcg_list_sets to find it.

name: ptcg_search_cards
title: Search Pokémon cards
